s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with mental confusion and generalized weakness
salient_findings: Progressive mental confusion over two months
Two left occipital lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI
key_facts: 54-year-old woman
Two-month history of progressive mental confusion
Marked worsening over the past two weeks
Complete dependence for basic activities of daily living
Well-controlled hypertension
Regular contact with various birds, including pigeons
Normotensive and in poor general condition
Able only to obey simple commands
Bedbound due to generalized weakness
No focal motor deficits
No cranial-nerve abnormalities
No meningeal signs
Karnofsky performance scale score of 50
Two left occipital lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive mental confusion and generalized weakness with brain lesions on MRI

shortlist.label: Glioblastoma multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of symptoms and presence of brain lesions

shortlist.label: Metastatic brain tumor
shortlist.why_kept: History of rapid decline and presence of multiple brain lesions

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Contact with birds and presence of brain lesions with surrounding edema

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of neurological decline with mental confusion and generalized weakness

raw.rationale: The patient's rapid decline and presence of two left occipital lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI are more suggestive of a metastatic brain tumor, especially given the lack of other systemic abnormalities or specific infectious or inflammatory signs

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: Less likely due to the presence of two distinct lesions and lack of immunocompromised state

rejected.label: Glioblastoma multiforme
rejected.why: Typically presents with a single, heterogeneous lesion and more often has a shorter history of symptoms

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: More commonly seen in immunocompromised patients and would not fully explain the patient's rapid decline and lack of other systemic signs

rejected.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more subacute progression of cognitive decline, myoclonus, and other specific neurological signs not mentioned in the case
